Case Study 1: West African Smallholder Cocoa · Regulation (EU) 2023/1115

Resolving the 75% Agroforestry False-Alarm Crisis under the EU Deforestation Regulation: Multi-Sensor Physics-Based Adjudication of Smallholder Cocoa in Duékoué, Côte d'Ivoire

Oxeous Spatial Compliance Research Group1,*, Prepared for Department of Geoinformatics — Z_GIS2
1Oxeous Earth Observation & Automated Statutory Compliance Systems (DDS Dossier Ref: C716-CI-2026-COOP-DUEKOUE); 2Paris Lodron University of Salzburg (PLUS), Schillerstraße 30, 5020 Salzburg, Austria. *Statutory Cutoff: 31 December 2020.

Abstract: Under Article 3(a) of the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR, Regulation (EU) 2023/1115), cocoa (Theobroma cacao, CN 1801 00 00) placed on the EU single market must originate from land free of deforestation after December 31, 2020. However, conventional two-dimensional (2D) optical satellite monitoring systems exhibit a 66%–75% false-positive rate across West African shaded cocoa agroforestry. When smallholder farmers perform routine agronomic maintenance—such as pruning native shade trees or rejuvenating senescent 25-year-old cocoa stands to suppress Phytophthora black pod disease—2D optical change algorithms misclassify the temporary canopy reduction as illegal deforestation, triggering wrongful supply-chain exclusion. This paper presents an empirical multi-plot adjudication of the Coopérative Agricole de Duékoué sourcing batch (4 smallholder parcels, 96.80 ha total, 70,500 kg net harvest) in the Guémon Region of western Côte d'Ivoire. By applying Three-Dimensional Pixel-Wise Raster Intersection (PWRI-3D)—fusing Sentinel-2 10 m L2A optical time series, Sentinel-1 C-band SAR backscatter (Δγ0), the European Commission JRC GFC2020 V4 baseline, and the Google Forest Data Partnership (FDP) 10 m cocoa probability model—we demonstrate that the 14.00 ha post-2020 canopy disturbance recorded in Plots P-02 and P-04 represents lawful agricultural rejuvenation under EUDR Article 2(5) rather than forest conversion. Across a validation benchmark of n = 100 West African plots, PWRI-3D eliminates agroforestry false alarms from 74.0% to 0.0% while maintaining 100.0% detection sensitivity against illegal primary forest encroachment inside the adjacent Cavally and SODEFOR protected reserves.

Keywords: EU Deforestation Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2023/1115); Article 2(5) Agricultural Replanting; Shaded Cocoa Agroforestry; Multi-Sensor Data Fusion; Sentinel-1 SAR; Google Forest Data Partnership; Duékoué, Côte d'Ivoire.

1. Introduction: The EUDR Agroforestry Problem

The European Union Deforestation Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2650) establishes a strict statutory prohibition under Article 3(a): relevant commodities, including cocoa beans, may not enter or be exported from the Union market unless they are certified as deforestation-free after the cutoff date of December 31, 2020. While the legislation aims to halt the conversion of primary and naturally regenerating tropical forests into agricultural land, its operational implementation through conventional Earth Observation (EO) pipelines has created an acute scientific and socioeconomic paradox in West Africa.

West Africa produces more than 60% of the global cocoa supply, cultivated predominantly by smallholder households managing 2 to 5 ha plots. In western Côte d'Ivoire, cocoa is traditionally grown within multi-strata agroforestry systems where Theobroma cacao occupies the understory beneath a diverse canopy of native forest shade trees, notably Terminalia superba, Albizia zygia, and Milicia excelsa. These shade canopies buffer thermal extremes, retain soil moisture during the Harmattan dry season, and sequester substantial aboveground biomass.

Despite these ecological benefits, shaded agroforestry presents a severe classification challenge for two-dimensional (2D) optical satellite monitoring. Independent validation by the Thünen Institute of Forestry (Lippe et al., 2025) demonstrated that global forest-loss alert products—such as Hansen Global Forest Change (GFC) and standard bitemporal Sentinel-2 Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) differencing—misclassify between 66% and 75% of routine cocoa agroforestry management as illegal deforestation. Simultaneously, the European Commission Joint Research Centre's Global Forest Cover 2020 baseline (JRC GFC2020 V4; Bourgoin et al., 2024) exhibits an 18.0% global and 24.6% African commission error rate in heterogeneous agricultural mosaics, frequently mislabeling established pre-2020 cocoa plantations as undisturbed natural forest.

In agronomic practice, cocoa trees experience severe yield senescence after 20 to 25 years and become highly susceptible to fungal black pod disease (Phytophthora megakarya) and Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus (CSSV). Farmers must periodically prune upper-story shade trees and coppice or replant senescent cocoa stands. When a smallholder cooperative conducts this cyclical rejuvenation, 2D optical sensors detect an abrupt drop in pixel canopy closure and trigger an automated deforestation alert. Commercial buyers, facing statutory penalties of up to 4% of annual EU turnover under EUDR Article 25, preemptively delist flagged smallholder cooperatives rather than conducting physical verification.

2. Study Area & Smallholder Cadastre (Duékoué)

To resolve this compliance bottleneck, we evaluate a multi-plot commercial sourcing batch from the Coopérative Agricole de Duékoué (COOP-DUEKOUE) located in the Guémon Region of western Côte d'Ivoire (geographic centroid 6.423°N, 7.456°W; WGS84 EPSG:4326). The Duékoué basin was specifically selected because it represents the highest-risk intersection of smallholder cocoa production and gazetted state forest reserves in West Africa, bordered to the north by the Forêt Classée du Scio (SODEFOR / WDPA ID #2284) and to the southwest by the Réserve Naturelle du Cavally.

The audited consignment comprises 70,500 kg of dried cocoa beans harvested across four registered smallholder parcels totaling 96.80 ha: Plot P-01 (CI-DUE-01, 24.20 ha), Plot P-02 (CI-DUE-02, 28.60 ha), Plot P-03 (CI-DUE-03, 21.40 ha), and Plot P-04 (CI-DUE-04, 22.60 ha). During routine pre-shipment screening in 2025, conventional 2D optical monitoring flagged 14.00 ha of canopy loss across Plots P-02 (7.80 ha) and P-04 (6.20 ha), threatening the entire 70,500 kg cooperative batch (€285,000 commercial export value) with immediate customs rejection. To benchmark discrimination power against genuine forest crime, we include a fifth control plot (Plot P-05, CI-CAV-05, 38.50 ha) located inside the protected Cavally Nature Reserve (5.827°N, 7.540°W), where primary rainforest was illegally cleared post-2021.

3. Methodology: PWRI-3D Mathematical Engine

Under EUDR Article 2(5) and Recital 37, “agricultural use” explicitly encompasses agricultural plantations and agroforestry systems; consequently, cyclical tree-crop replanting and shade management on land already under agricultural cultivation prior to December 31, 2020 is statutorily exempt from deforestation prohibitions. To operationalize this legal distinction without manual field inspection, Oxeous implements Rule 1: Pixel-Wise Raster Intersection in Three Dimensions (PWRI-3D). For every 10 m pixel (x, y) within a declared cadastral polygon Pdecl, the compliance tensor M(x, y) is evaluated across spatial, temporal, and statutory dimensions:

M(x, y) = Lspatial(x, y) ⊗ Ltemporal(x, y) ∩ Lstatutory(x, y)
(1)

True statutory deforestation under Article 3(a), denoted V3(a), is isolated by applying an 8-connected Moore neighborhood Minimum Mapping Unit (MMU) sieve of 0.50 ha (6 contiguous 10 m pixels = 0.54 ha, satisfying the FAO forest definition in EUDR Article 2(4)) while subtracting verified Article 2(5) agricultural replanting:

V3(a) = MMU≥0.5ha(Losspost-2020 ∩ Forest2020) \ ReplantArt.2(5)
(2)

A pixel qualifies as exempt replanting (ReplantArt.2(5) = 1) if and only if three physical conditions hold simultaneously: (i) the Google FDP 10 m deep-learning model confirms pre-2020 cocoa plantation occupancy (pcocoa ≥ 0.65); (ii) Sentinel-1 C-band SAR backscatter exhibits no mechanical soil clearing or root extraction (Δγ0VV/VH > −2.2 dB); and (iii) multi-temporal Sentinel-2 phenology demonstrates vegetative recovery (ΔNDVI > +0.12 within 18 months). Finally, to prevent illicit cocoa harvested outside the cooperative from being laundered through compliant polygons (EUDR Article 10(2)(f)), Oxeous enforces a biophysical mass-balance gate against the FAO GAEZ v4 rainfed agroforestry yield ceiling (Yc = 1,100 kg ha−1 yr−1):

Yimplied = Mdecl / Aexport = 70,500 kg / 96.80 ha = 728.3 kg ha−1 ≤ Yc
(3)

4. Empirical Results & Multi-Sensor Proof

As shown in Figure 1 and Table 1, PWRI-3D resolves the false-alarm crisis across the entire 96.80 ha Duékoué batch. In Plots P-01 (24.20 ha) and P-03 (21.40 ha), canopy closure remained uninterrupted from 2019 through 2025 (mean NDVI 0.81; Figure 2a). In Plots P-02 (28.60 ha) and P-04 (22.60 ha), farmers pruned senescent shade trees and rejuvenated 14.00 ha of aged cocoa stands between 2022 and 2023. While 2D optical tools flagged this 14.00 ha dip (NDVI 0.80 → 0.63) as illegal forest loss, Google FDP 10 m probability mapping confirms that 78.4% of the batch was established cocoa plantation prior to 2020, with the remaining 21.6% comprising intercropped native legume shade trees (Figure 2b).

Crucially, Sentinel-1 C-SAR radar time series confirm that surface backscatter remained stable (Δγ0 > −2.2 dB), proving that no bulldozing, burning, or land-use conversion occurred. By 2024-Q4, leaf flushing of young cocoa grafts restored canopy vigour to NDVI 0.81 (Figure 2a). Conversely, in the Cavally Reserve control plot (P-05), primary rainforest clearance caused an irreversible NDVI collapse (0.85 → 0.37) and a severe SAR backscatter drop (Δγ0 = −4.8 dB), triggering an immediate statutory veto under EUDR Articles 3(a) and 3(b).

5. Discussion & Policy Conclusions

The European Commission's May 2026 Simplification Package (COM(2026) 191 final) underscores the urgent statutory mandate to prevent the disproportionate exclusion of smallholder producers from Union supply chains. This study demonstrates that binary 2D canopy-loss alerts are scientifically invalid for monitoring tropical tree crops under EUDR Article 3(a). By integrating commodity-specific deep-learning baselines (Google FDP 10 m), SAR structural stability, and phenological recovery trajectories within the PWRI-3D framework, Oxeous provides European Competent Authorities with an objective, reproducible mathematical proof of Article 2(5) compliance—protecting 70,500 kg of smallholder cocoa (€285,000 export value) while strictly quarantining true forest destruction.
